task_set.title: Bigville adapter navigation retrieval probes
task_set.provenance: Six frozen tasks selected from distinct Bigville scenario, seed-dependency, generated-seed, pack, and route examples. Expected paths are the source records at the ends of the requested navigation; representative graph relationships are independently asserted by navigation_eval.py.

arm_descriptions.baseline: Plain source-file listing, sorted by path, truncated to budget.
arm_descriptions.dev_context: DevMemory.context items/snippets, executed at the budget.
arm_descriptions.dev_repo_map: Ranked repo map, executed at the budget.
arm_descriptions.both: Union of the dev_context and dev_repo_map file sets.
arm_descriptions.grep: Lexical baseline: files ranked by distinct task terms found in their text, then total occurrences, then path.
arm_descriptions.code_search: ozagia.core.search.code_search results, rendered as path:line: snippet in result order, truncated to budget.

tasks.task: For the house argument scenario, locate its conversation knowledge definition and determine which source copy the runtime reference can mean.
tasks.notes: Exercises scenario-to-seed navigation and path-distinct duplicate ID handling.

tasks.task: Trace the generated council charter knowledge back to the authored pack table and identify the declared source provenance.
tasks.notes: Exercises generated seed to pack table provenance navigation.

tasks.task: Find the authored terrain movement rules table that produced the packaged terrain movement knowledge, including its pack declaration.
tasks.notes: Second generated seed/table example from a different pack domain.

tasks.task: The packaged bell schedule declares a dependency on shared bell knowledge. Find every available manifest for that dependency and determine whether the ID selects one copy.
tasks.notes: Exercises a manifest dependency edge with duplicate path-distinct target IDs.

tasks.task: For the four player Monopoly scenario, find both conversation manifests and both conversation reply manifests that its ID-only seed references can resolve to.
tasks.notes: Second scenario exercises ambiguity across two seed IDs rather than one reference.

tasks.task: Trace the management browser's backend profile listing request to the server handler that implements the same HTTP endpoint.
tasks.notes: Exercises explicit browser request to server route joining.

`bigville/management/static/management.js` | Exercises explicit browser request to server route joining. | ## Reading these numbers - This is a **retrieval instrument**, not an end-to-end coding benchmark: it measures whether known-relevant files are selected, not whether an agent completes a change. - `baseline` is a sorted-path file-listing control, not a semantic retriever. `grep` is a lexical control: it counts distinct task words found in each file's text. - `recall` counts a hit at any tier. `recall_content` counts only hits whose file the arm showed as code (code_search snippet, dev_context item with snippet text, or repo-map `full`/`outline` tier). A listing-tier hit tells the reader the path exists, not what it contains. - Token estimates are each module's own ~4-chars/token heuristic. Cache counts apply only to repo-map arms. - `both` is the literal union of the two retrievers run at the same budget; its token cost and latency are the sum of the components, so its budget is per component (up to 2x the nominal budget). Compare it as a cost/recall trade-off, not as an equal-token arm. - `code_search` runs once per task; its elapsed time is the same call's time at every budget. - Ground truth is frozen in the task JSON. Re-run the scoped tests after moving or renaming an expected file.
